title: Reading Windows Performance in Task Manager
overview: Task Manager provides a live view of the applications and Windows processes using processor, memory, disk, and network resources. The goal is to observe sustained patterns before making a change—not to end unfamiliar processes.
checklist: Wait about 30 seconds so brief startup spikes can settle.
Select a CPU, Memory, or Disk column to identify the busiest processes.
Confirm that a process is an application you recognize before closing it.
Use Startup apps to review impact, but disable an item only after confirming that it is optional and understanding what it does.
common_indicators: CPU remains near full utilization even when the computer is idle.
Memory stays very high while applications pause or reload.
Disk remains at or near full activity for several minutes.
Performance improves when a known, unused application is closed.
The computer is slow mainly during the first few minutes after sign-in.

commands.description: Use tasklist to gather supporting diagnostic information.
Use systeminfo to gather supporting diagnostic information.

quiz.question: What should you do before ending a process in Task Manager?
answers: Confirm it is an application you recognize
